symptom: Desktop RC validation can spend release time validating and packaging a commit different from the workflow trigger commit.
direct_cause: The workflow checked out inputs.ref without comparing its resolved commit with github.sha before validation.
class_root: The RC workflow had no first shared source identity boundary tying the requested ref to the triggering commit.
affected_population: workflow_dispatch RC runs where inputs.ref differs from the triggering ref or commit
entry_points: Desktop Release Candidate workflow_dispatch validate job
internal_only_reason: This is an internal GitHub Actions source identity invariant; repository workflow and lesson history define the required boundary.
invariants: The commit resolved from inputs.ref must equal github.sha before any RC validation, packaging, or test step runs.

door_reduction.why_not: The resolver and comparator are separate shared boundary operations and both must remain explicit.

generality_proof: Every RC workflow_dispatch run enters through the validate job and now crosses the same comparison script before installation or downstream jobs receive its SHA.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Fail closed unless the requested ref commit and github.sha are identical, while reporting trigger context.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The first post-checkout step invokes verify-workflow-ref.mjs with inputs.ref and github.sha.
Promotion consumes the immutable RC manifest SHA and does not checkout an operator-selected validation ref.

recurrence.reason: Any future dispatch can select a ref different from the trigger commit and otherwise waste the full RC run before discovering the drift.
same_class_scan: Scanned .github/workflows/desktop-rc.yml inputs.ref and all downstream ref checkouts.
Checked docs/lessons/rc-must-be-dispatched-on-the-release-branch.md for the recorded source drift class.

prevention.invariant: Resolved inputs.ref SHA equals github.sha before RC work begins.
prevention.failure_mode: The validate job exits nonzero with trigger ref, intended ref, resolved SHA, and github SHA.
prevention.strategy: Keep one script as the only comparison implementation and call it as the first post-checkout validate step.

legacy_paths.rationale: No parallel identity checker existed; the missing comparison is added at the existing validate boundary.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party runtime controls this internal workflow invariant.

migration: No stored data or user state changes; future RC dispatches fail early when identity is inconsistent.
residual_risks: GitHub Actions must provide a resolvable github.sha and a fetched inputs.ref; checkout fetch-depth remains 0 to preserve that boundary.
